import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert date to datetime
df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive analysis
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Coffee Shop Sales Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Color palette
colors = sns.color_palette('viridis', n_colors=10)

# 1. Top Products by Total Revenue
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
product_revenue = df.groupby('product')['total'].sum().sort_values(ascending=True)
bars = ax1.barh(product_revenue.index, product_revenue.values, color=sns.color_palette('viridis', len(product_revenue)))
ax1.set_xlabel('Total Revenue ($)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Product', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Total Revenue by Product', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
for i, (bar, val) in enumerate(zip(bars, product_revenue.values)):
    ax1.text(val + 50, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, f'${val:,.0f}', va='center', fontsize=9)

# 2. Sales by Customer Age Group and Payment Method
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
age_payment = df.groupby(['customer_age_group', 'payment_method'])['total'].sum().unstack(fill_value=0)
# Order age groups logically
age_order = ['18-24', '25-34', '35-44', '45-54', '55+']
age_payment = age_payment.reindex([a for a in age_order if a in age_payment.index])
age_payment.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax2, color=sns.color_palette('Set2', len(age_payment.columns)), width=0.8)
ax2.set_xlabel('Customer Age Group', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Total Revenue ($)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Revenue by Age Group & Payment Method', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax2.legend(title='Payment Method', loc='upper right', fontsize=9)
ax2.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=0)

# 3. Price Distribution by Size
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
size_order = ['Small', 'Medium', 'Large']
df['size'] = pd.Categorical(df['size'], categories=size_order, ordered=True)
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='size', y='price', ax=ax3, palette='coolwarm', order=size_order)
ax3.set_xlabel('Size', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Price ($)', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Price Distribution by Size', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')

# Add mean markers
means = df.groupby('size')['price'].mean()
for i, size in enumerate(size_order):
    if size in means.index:
        ax3.scatter(i, means[size], color='red', s=100, zorder=5, marker='D', label='Mean' if i == 0 else '')
ax3.legend(loc='upper left')

# 4. Dine-in vs Takeaway by Product
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
takeaway_product = df.groupby(['product', 'is_takeaway'])['total'].sum().unstack(fill_value=0)
takeaway_product.columns = ['Dine-in', 'Takeaway']
takeaway_product = takeaway_product.sort_values('Takeaway', ascending=True)
takeaway_product.plot(kind='barh', ax=ax4, color=['#2ecc71', '#e74c3c'], width=0.8, stacked=True)
ax4.set_xlabel('Total Revenue ($)', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Product', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Dine-in vs Takeaway Revenue by Product', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(title='Order Type', loc='lower right', fontsize=9)

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
